ss-delta 0.5.0 unlocks all eight Blank Page slots and makes pact pages with "Sacrifice memory" again, adds the original game's Spirits' offerings and PS TV controls, and fixes Blitz offerings and loading screens at 60 fps. It also fixes the setup for games copied from your own Vita and for the update on Linux and the Steam Deck.

## Downloads

| System | Download | Start |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11, x64 | `ss-delta-v0.5.0-windows.zip` | `ss-delta.exe` |
| Linux x64, Steam Deck | `ss-delta-v0.5.0-linux.tar.gz` | `ss-delta.x86_64` |
| macOS 13.3+ on Apple Silicon | `ss-delta-v0.5.0-macos.tar.gz` | `Soul Sacrifice Delta.app` |
| Android 9+, 64-bit ARM with Vulkan | `ss-delta-v0.5.0-android.apk` | **ss-delta** (install the APK) |

On a PC, unpack the archive and start the game. The first time, its importer asks for your own dump of Soul Sacrifice Delta (US PCSA00152 or EU PCSF00532, update 1.30), downloads the PS Vita firmware from Sony and a compiler, and builds the game on your computer in a few minutes. From then on the program goes straight to the game. Nothing of the game is in these downloads. See the [installation guide](https://github.com/vita-recomps/ss-delta/blob/main/docs/INSTALLING.md).

macOS: the app isn't signed by a registered Apple developer, so macOS refuses it the first time. Open System Settings, Privacy & Security, and click "Open Anyway".

## New

* **All eight Blank Page slots** ([#15](https://github.com/vita-recomps/ss-delta/issues/15)). Librom's Blank Page has eight slots for created pact pages, and only three are open in any save. The other five were unlocked with Memory Clods, bought on the PlayStation Store. With Add-ons (DLC) on, ss-delta unlocks them in your save, and the game keeps them when it saves.
* **"Sacrifice memory" works again** (#15). Creating a page with a Memory Clod instead of an Offering, which gives Complete Victory rewards you don't own yet, needed the PlayStation Store. With Add-ons on it now costs nothing. Blank Page pacts also work in Ad Hoc Play: the host picks one from Select Quest's Blank Page tab.
* **The original game's Spirits' offerings** ([#11](https://github.com/vita-recomps/ss-delta/issues/11)): the 20 pre-order offerings of the first *Soul Sacrifice* (Spirits' Flamepike ... Spirits' Gravelshield). Delta still has them, switched off; ss-delta switches them on and gives each once per save, with Add-ons on. They look and play like Delta's own offerings of the same kind. No copy of the original is needed.
* **PS TV controls** ([#12](https://github.com/vita-recomps/ss-delta/issues/12)), on the settings menu's Game page: the game runs as a PlayStation TV, which has no touchscreen. The one touch the story needs, pulling Librom out of the bones at the start of a new game, then takes L2 or R2 (the gamepad's triggers).

## Fixed

* **Blitz offerings at 60 fps** ([#14](https://github.com/vita-recomps/ss-delta/issues/14)). After a hit, a Blitz offering's push-back moved you a fixed step every frame, so at 60 fps it threw you almost twice as far as on the Vita and the next cast of a chain fell short. It now plays at 60 as it does at 30.
* **Loading screens run at 60 fps.** The quest-start loading screen could hang at 60 fps, so loading screens were kept at 30. The hang was a race in the game itself, now fixed, so loading screens run at your frame rate.
* **Games copied straight off a Vita** ([#13](https://github.com/vita-recomps/ss-delta/issues/13)). The game's folder on a Vita carries your PSN account's own licence, which works only on that Vita, so the setup stopped with "header signature is invalid". It now says so before downloading anything. It needs the licence NoNpDrm writes (`ux0:nonpdrm/license/...`): copy that `license` folder next to `app/` and `patch/`, or give the `.rif` as the game's licence, which is now used for a folder or `.zip` too. See "From your own Vita" in the [installation guide](https://github.com/vita-recomps/ss-delta/blob/main/docs/INSTALLING.md#what-you-need).
* **Linux and the Steam Deck: the update could be left out** (#13). With the game and its update in one folder (`app/` and `patch/`), the setup could install the update first, fail, and stop with "eboot.bin is not a build this port supports". The game is now always installed first, and the setup says plainly when the update is missing.
* A folder whose game failed to install no longer counts as installed because something else in it did; the setup shows the real reason instead of "no PCSA00152 or PCSF00532 ... after installing".
* Removing a packaged mod that had added a table the game's patch archive lacks no longer leaves a copy of the archive behind.

## Upgrading from 0.4.x

Build the game again for this release: the Blitz and loading-screen fixes are in the game's recompiled code. Unpack 0.5.0 over your game's folder (replace the files) and start it with `--install`, or update through RecompLauncher, which builds the game again from your dump by itself. Saves and settings are kept. A game built by 0.4.x still runs with 0.5.0, but without those two fixes, and its loading screens stay at 30 fps. Coming from 0.3 or older, see [Updating](https://github.com/vita-recomps/ss-delta/blob/main/docs/INSTALLING.md#updating).

Every release's changes: [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/vita-recomps/ss-delta/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

SHA-256 and build attestations: see the files attached, and `gh attestation verify`.
